extracted.intended_audience: empirical legal scholars, economists, patent policy researchers, and USPTO policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical analysis of patent examiners' time allocation (procrastination/end-loading), how to measure it using FOAM timing, and the consequences for examination quality and duration. Includes econometric specifications, controls, event-study tests (telecommuting), and assessments of alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOAM (First Office Action on the Merits) timing / end-loading
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure completion timing of FOAMs by day and detect bunching (end-loading) at the end of bi-weekly quota periods; example evidence: 26 evenly spaced spikes corresponding to bi-week ends and nearly half of FOAMs completed on the last day of a quota period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct histograms (representative year and pooled 14-day prior-to-deadline averaging). Account for weekend dips. Compare daily frequencies across the bi-week period to identify end-of-period spikes; end-loading is operationalized as clustering of FOAM completions on the final day(s) of quota windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: FOAM
rubrics_metrics.description: FOAM refers to the first office action associated with a given application (first office action on the merits). The first office action after filing an RCE may be viewed technically as a FOAM but is treated as distinct in this analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endloaded indicator (binary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator variable equal to one if the FOAM was completed on the last day of the bi-weekly quota period (used to flag end-of-period reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the main treatment variable in regressions examining allowance, subsequent rejections, RCEs, duration, and cross-office outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark of non-procrastinator vs procrastinator work path
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-procrastinating examiner expected to smooth work efforts within a bi-week period; a procrastinating examiner is predicted to bunch work efforts near the end of the period (end-load).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This behavioral benchmark motivates comparison of observed daily FOAM completion distributions to the smoothing pattern; theoretical reference to O’Donoghue and Rabin (hyperbolic discounting) and a model in the Online Appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOAM allowance rate as a quality marker (shotgun rejections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare FOAM allowance rates for applications reviewed at quota ends versus within-quota periods; substantially lower FOAM allowance rates at quota-ends are interpreted as evidence of 'shotgun' (quick, low-quality) rejections driven by time pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regression specification (Equation (1)) estimates FOAM_Allowait = α + γ_i + λ_t + β1 Endloaded_ait + β2 X_ait + ε_ait with examiner and year fixed effects. On average, an examiner allows on the FOAM roughly 10 percentage points lower when reviewing on the last day of a quota period (text reports this as 'roughly 10 percentage-point lower—or a nearly 87 percent lower rate').

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner fixed-effects specification and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Use examiner fixed effects and year fixed effects in regressions to compare an examiner’s outcomes at quota-ends versus within-quota periods while controlling for application characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls (X_ait) include: examiner GS pay level, examiner experience (2-year bins), technology groups (37 NBER sub-categories), large-entity applicant dummy, foreign priority dummy (JPO/EPO). Standard errors clustered by examiner. Consider instrumental variables modification for unobservables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with examiner mean end-loading rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether the negative relationship between end-loading and FOAM allowances is stronger for examiners with higher overall end-loading rates by interacting application-level end-loading with the examiner’s mean end-loading rate (excluding the focal application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate modified specification including the interaction term; a negative coefficient on the interaction provides evidence that time-crunch effects are concentrated among high end-loaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second non-final rejection incidence as indicator of low-quality FOAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the incidence of a second non-final office action rejection as a marker of low-quality initial review (the PTO views second non-final rejections as indicative of incomplete initial review). Applications rejected in an end-loaded FOAM are ~1.4–2 percentage points (≈8–12%) more likely to receive a second non-final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate on the sample of applications undergoing subsequent rounds; interpret higher second non-final rates for end-loaded FOAMs as consistent with shotgun rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate allowance probability (final disposition) as outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether end-loading of the FOAM affects the likelihood the application is ultimately allowed by final disposition; end-loaded FOAMs are associated with a smaller negative effect (~1.8 percentage points, ~2.5%) on ultimate allowance than the FOAM-level gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace FOAM allowance dependent variable with ultimate-allowance indicator in the same specification to compare magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-office validity benchmark (EPO & JPO outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use whether a U.S.-issued patent was also allowed at both the EPO and the JPO as an external benchmark of legal validity. Find a 0.6 percentage-point (~1.3%) reduction in the likelihood of being allowed at both foreign offices when the U.S. FOAM was end-loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat EPO/JPO joint allowance as an imperfect but informative proxy for substantive validity; interpret small negative effects as modest quality deterioration from end-loading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination prolongation metrics: RCE incidence, number of RCEs, and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether end-loading on FOAM is associated with prolonging the examination process via: (1) incidence of a Request for Continued Examination (RCE), (2) number of RCEs filed, and (3) duration in days of the examination period. Findings: end-loaded FOAMs are ~2.4 percentage points (~10%) more likely to have an RCE, associated with a 12% increase in number of RCEs, and an average increase of 50 days in examination duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate appropriate regressions with the same fixed effects and controls; interpret increases in these metrics as evidence that procrastination-induced shotgun rejections can prolong prosecution and backlog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecommuting (Patents Hoteling Program) event-study test
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how an examiner’s commencement of telecommuting (PHP) affects end-loading. Use event-time dummies for r = -4..4 years around start of telecommuting in an examiner fixed-effects framework. Joining PHP increases end-loading by 7 percentage points (~14%) immediately upon joining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dynamic difference-in-differences design using examiners who do not switch as controls; plot coefficients of event-time indicators. Also test interaction of event-time with quota-end indicator to see whether FOAM allowance differentials intensify after telecommuting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declining end-loading across successive office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare end-loading intensity across stages: FOAM shows strongest end-loading (~50% last-day), second office action weaker (~35% last-day), third office action substantially weaker (~11% last-day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret decline as consistent with fixed-costs concentrated in early stages and the predictions of multi-stage procrastination models (e.g., O’Donoghue & Rabin). Replicate histograms conditioning on stage of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shotgun rejection concept and operational markers
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'shotgun rejection' refers to examiners rejecting claims for 'questionable reasons' under time pressure. Operational markers: lower FOAM allowance rates at quota-ends, higher second non-final rejection rates, increased subsequent scrutiny/corrections in later rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use within-examiner comparisons and event-study evidence (telecommuting interaction) to link shotgun rejections to time-crunch mechanisms rather than permanent leniency differences across examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and rejection of alternative time-consistent explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and rule out alternative explanations for end-loading: (1) Paper Pile (accumulating work and filing in bunches), (2) Supervisor Effect (delays due to supervisory sign-off), and (3) Application Sorting by complexity. The paper-pile and supervisor explanations are inconsistent with observed quarter spikes, telecommuting effects, shotgun markers, and persistent end-loading among examiners with sign-off authority; sorting would require an implausible distribution of application complexities and does not explain shotgun markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform falsification checks: compare treated vs control trends around telecommuting, assess end-loading among examiners with independent sign-off authority (Table A2 shows ~44% end-loading), and reason with institutional time limits and observed patterns across quarters and stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard errors clustering and robustness considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cluster standard errors to correct for autocorrelation within examiners over time. Consider instrumental variables modifications and additional falsification exercises (e.g., immutable application characteristics stability) to bolster causal claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cluster by examiner. Use examiner fixed effects, year fixed effects, event-study dynamics, and balance/falsification checks (e.g., applicant entity size and foreign priority status year-by-year around telecommuting onset) to address confounding and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational sample construction and averaging scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing day-relative-to-quota histograms, average FOAM counts for all calendar dates that fell X days prior to a bi-weekly deadline (e.g., 13 days prior, 12 days prior, etc.) over the full sample period (2002-2012) to produce generalized histograms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This averaging smooths calendar effects and isolates within-quota-day patterns; be mindful of weekend effects and quarter boundaries.
